verdict.rationale: Jitsu ships an official `jitsu-cli` that manages workspace configuration objects (destinations, streams, connections) and runs the Functions dev workflow, including `init` scaffolding and `deploy`. It saves credentials for non-interactive use and is described as doing everything the UI does; a probe confirms its official docs page. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the CLI in practice, and documentation of agent-friendly specifics such as machine-readable output.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: `jitsu-cli` is the command-line interface for Jitsu. It manages workspace configuration objects (destinations, streams, connections, …) and runs the Functions dev workflow.
**`jitsu-cli`** — a real command-line interface that does everything the UI does.
`jitsu-cli init` scaffolds a TypeScript project with tests, and `jitsu-cli deploy` ships it to your workspace.
Saves credentials so subsequent commands don't need `-h` / `-k`.
